parole.testo: A combination of Latin ballare and a family of Middle French words beginning in *brimb-, esp. brimber (“to beg”), which give the sense of "wandering to and fro". Borrowed from Latin dēsōlātiōnem f or derived from Middle French desolation f.
From Old French honesté, from Latin honestātem, reshaped as if from honnête + -té starting from Middle French honesteté. Compare Spanish honestidad and Portuguese honestidade.
Inherited from Middle French entention, from Old French entencion, borrowed from Latin intentiōnem. Respelled intention in Middle French to more closely match the Classical Latin form.

parole.significato: to offend (to insult, to cause offence)
parole.testo: From offense + -er, from Latin offēnsāre (“to strike against”), replacing previous Middle French offendre.
